item.title: Here's why an Arizona medical examiner is working to track heat-related deaths
item.description: No one across the U.S. is consistently tracking climate-fueled deaths. One medical examiner has a new protocol on heat-deaths.

item.title: Committee investigating Epstein holds billionaire Leon Black in contempt of Congress
item.description: Billionaire investor Leon Black refused to appear before the committee investigating convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein for a deposition. Now it's up to the Department of Justice whether to pursue criminal charges.

item.title: Cash aid can lead to improved financial circumstance, but can also increase conflict
item.description: In Liberia, the government gave cash transfers to couples to see if it would help solve problems that arise when partners disagree about how to manage money.

item.title: A look at the secretive unit inside Department of Homeland Security
item.description: NPR's Mary Louise Kelly talks with the reporter of a story that shows how the Department of Homeland Security is feeding information to local police as part of DHS' Predictive Intelligence Unit.

item.title: Fed raises interest rates for first time in more than three years
item.description: The Federal Reserve raised interest rates today Wednesday the first time in more than three years. The central bank is trying to curb stubborn inflation, which was rekindled by the war with Iran.

item.description: Gene technology is giving hope to citrus farmers in Florida who are fighting greening disease, which has been killing their trees for two decades.
